metadata.note: Modern-day Long Island Rail Road network, as of the GTFS feed pulled from http://rrgtfsfeeds.s3.amazonaws.com/gtfslirr.zip. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/amtrak.geojson. Each route is a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added by estimating headway_min at researched ownership/frequency-milestone boundaries (predecessor-railroad origin dates, 1900 Pennsylvania RR acquisition, 1905-1926 electrification of individual branches, 1966 State of New York purchase / 1968 MTA control, etc., sourced from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites); unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, these older headway numbers are not derived from real historical timetables and should be read as illustrative estimates, not precise data.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.port_jefferson_extension: 2026-09-28: the Port Jefferson Branch had been drawn only to Huntington, because the GTFS pipeline took the most common trip pattern (the electric Huntington trains). Added the missing 22.7 mi as lirr-14/15 (traced from OSM, checked against GTFS trip counts), plus the Northport Branch (lirr-16, passenger years 1868–1899 only), the Wading River extension (lirr-17, 1895–1938) and Hicksville–Syosset before 1868 (lirr-18). lirr-10 now starts in 1868, the year it reached Huntington, instead of 1873. Only passenger years are drawn: the Northport Branch's freight years (1899–1978) and the Kings Park Psychiatric Center spur are left off.
not_yet_sourced: Wading River extension: a reader reports that the rails were pulled during WWII; the station histories say the line was abandoned in 1938. The drawn years end at the Oct 9 1938 abandonment either way, but when the track was lifted is unresolved.
Wading River extension: documented route mileage not checked against the traced 11.4 mi.
Smithtown & Port Jefferson Railroad (1873–1892): not confirmed that the LIRR operated it from opening. If the S&PJ ran its own trains, lirr-15 needs splitting at the date the LIRR took over (Rule 4).
Hicksville & Syosset Railroad (1854–1868): operator not confirmed; drawn as LIRR.
Kings Park Psychiatric Center spur: carried Sunday passengers from 1896 by one account; years not sourced, so not drawn.
All headways before 2026 on lirr-14 through lirr-18 are estimates.
